title: Global components of a labelled etale coordinate boundary
statement: Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Let $E,F_1,\ldots,F_m\hookrightarrow Y$ be reduced closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], with $m\ge0$, and suppose the $F_a$ are nonempty, pairwise distinct and irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $C\hookrightarrow Y$ be a reduced closed subscheme containing $E$ and every $F_a$, and let $D=(E\cup\bigcup_a F_a)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Suppose that for every $y\in Y$ there exist an actual etale morphism $v:V\to Y$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and $z\in V$ above $y$, with $\mathcal O_{V,z}$ a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] having a regular system of parameters $s_1,\ldots,s_d$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Assume that in this local scheme every member of the labelled family $E,F_1,\ldots,F_m$ is empty or one coordinate hyperplane $V(s_i)$, with different nonempty members assigned different indices. Assume also that the reduced pullback of $C$ has equation $\prod_{i\in K}s_i=0$ for a subset $K\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$ containing every assigned index. Every intersection of $q$ distinct coordinate hyperplanes in these equations is required to be empty or regular, with every irreducible component of codimension $q$ in $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{V,z}$; the empty intersection is this local scheme. Then $Y$ is regular, $E$ and each $F_a$ are regular, and $C$ and $D$ are effective Cartier divisors [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. The divisor $C$ has normal crossings [def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor]. The irreducible components of $E$ are finite and pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes of $E$; the irreducible components of $D$ are exactly these components and the $F_a$, with their reduced structures. Every intersection of $q$ distinct components of $D$ is empty or regular of codimension $q$ in $Y$. Thus $D$ is a strict normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] and a union of irreducible components of $C$ [def-trf-union-of-irreducible-components]. Empty $Y$, $E$, $C$, $D$, the empty labelled family, and disconnected $E$ are permitted.

source.place: Expose VIII 4.1.2--4.1.4(i), printed p. 117; Lemma 4.2.9 and its coordinate-chart proof, printed p. 121; the regular-intersection criterion is Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118.

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$ and a stipulated chart $(V,z)$, and put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $R=\mathcal O_{V,z}$. Apply [lem-trf-finite-intersection-etale-stalk-model] with the empty subset: $A\to R$ is a flat local map of Noetherian local rings. Since $R$ is regular, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular] makes $A$ regular. For a label $L\in\{E,F_1,\ldots,F_m\}$ and $y\in L$, the same model identifies its stalk with $A/I_L$ and gives a flat local map $A/I_L\to R/I_LR$. Here $I_LR=(s_i)$ for its assigned index. By [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters](b), $R/(s_i)$ is regular local. A second application of flat descent makes $A/I_L$ regular. The model also gives local Noetherianity of each $L$. Thus every stalk of $Y,E,F_a$ is regular, which is exactly [def-weil-regular-scheme]; points outside a label require no stalk check.

source.place: Tag 00OF, lemma-flat-under-regular; etale.tex Tag 025N, proposition-etale-regular; ILO VIII 4.1.4(i).

proof.text: The closed subscheme $E$ is quasi-compact: add $Y\setminus E$ to an open cover of $E$ and use quasi-compactness of $Y$. Together with step 1 this makes $E$ Noetherian. Apply [rem-pc-regular-normal](1)--(2) to $E$: its finitely many irreducible components $E_b$ are disjoint and open and closed in $E$, and integral. Each is regular because its local rings are those of $E$. Apply the same node to $Y$: its irreducible components are also open and closed. Each $F_a$ is integral because it is reduced and nonempty irreducible, by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. For a fixed $y$, any $E_b$ not containing $y$ has empty pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}R$, since its closed ideal becomes the unit ideal at $y$. If $y\in E$, exactly one $E_b$ contains it. The other finitely many components disappear in that local scheme, so the surviving $E_b$ has exactly the coordinate equation assigned to $E$. Thus the refined family $\mathcal G=(E_b)_b,(F_a)_a$ still consists locally of distinct labelled coordinate hyperplanes or empty subschemes.

source.place: VIII 4.1.4(i), 4.2.2(i); properties.tex Tags 0569 and 033M, regularity-normality and normal Noetherian decomposition.

proof.text: For any subset $J$ of the finite refined family $\mathcal G$, its local scheme-theoretic intersection is empty if one selected member is empty. Otherwise the equations are $s_{i(G)}=0$ for $G\in J$, at $|J|$ distinct indices; this is an equality of ideals, not just of supports. The empty subset gives $\operatorname{Spec}R$. The assumed regular-intersection condition supplies regularity and component codimension $|J|$ in each of these local schemes. Apply [lem-trf-etale-regular-intersection-descent] to $X=Y$ and the family $\mathcal G$. It gives regularity of every global scheme-theoretic intersection and codimension $|J|$ for each of its irreducible components. This includes singleton intersections and the empty subset. The same actual etale chart may be used for every $J$ at a given $y$; a global labelling of the etale branches of $C$ is unnecessary.

source.place: VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), regular-intersection criterion; etale.tex Tags 025N and 039S.

proof.text: We also need the local dimension equality, not only generic component codimension. Let $y\in G_J=\bigcap_{G\in J}G$. By [lem-trf-finite-intersection-etale-stalk-model], its pulled-back stalk is $R/(s_{i(G)}:G\in J)$. By [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters](b), its dimension is $\dim R-|J|$. Apply [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension] to $V\to Y$ on affine neighbourhoods of $z,y$ to obtain $\dim R=\dim A$. The morphism $G_J\times_YV\to G_J$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Applying the same local-dimension lemma on affine neighbourhoods for this morphism gives $\dim\mathcal O_{G_J,y}=\dim R/(s_{i(G)}:G\in J)$. Hence $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}=\dim\mathcal O_{G_J,y}+|J|$. These are applications to actual etale morphisms before taking local rings; no finite-presentation assertion about the map between stalks is needed.

source.place: Tag 07QP, lemma-dimension-etale-extension; morphisms.tex Tag 02GO, lemma-base-change-etale; etale.tex Tag 0BIA, lemma-strict-normal-crossings.

proof.text: The actual pullbacks $C\times_YV$ and $D\times_YV$ are reduced by the first assertion of [lem-trf-etale-reduced-cartier-descent]. Indeed $C,D$ are reduced closed subschemes, so by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](3) they are the reduced induced structures on their supports. Thus in $R$ the ideal of $C$ is the stipulated $(\prod_{i\in K}s_i)$, even though the hypothesis initially describes its reduced pullback. For $D$, its local support is the union of the hyperplanes assigned to the labels: inverse image commutes with finite union. Its ideal is therefore the intersection of their prime ideals, since the pullback is reduced. By [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters](b), this intersection is $(\prod_{i\in H}s_i)$, where $H$ is the set of assigned indices. Both products are nonzerodivisors; the empty product is $1$. Consequently both local pullbacks are effective Cartier divisors on $\operatorname{Spec}R$.

source.place: VIII 4.1.2 and Lemma 4.2.9; descent.tex Tag 034E, lemma-reduced-local-smooth; schemes.tex Tag 01J3, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme.

proof.text: For either ideal $I=I_C$ or $I_D$ in $A$, the flat local map $A\to R$ is faithfully flat, with surjective spectrum, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat]. The single affine morphism $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an fpqc cover: it is flat and surjective, and inverse images of basic affine opens are affine, so the covering condition in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] holds. Step 5 says its pulled-back closed ideal is effective Cartier. Apply [lem-trf-fpqc-cartier-ideal-reflection] to $V(I)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A$. It follows that $I$ is effective Cartier; at the closed point of this local scheme it is generated by a nonzerodivisor. Do this at every $y$. By [lem-sfb-stalk-nonzerodivisor-cartier-spreading], these stalk generators give effective Cartier ideals on $Y$. Thus $C$ and $D$ are effective Cartier divisors, including their empty cases.

source.place: Tag 05B2, lemma-finite-locally-free-descends; divisors.tex Tag 0AG8, lemma-effective-Cartier-in-points; algebra.tex Tag 00HR, lemma-local-flat-ff.

proof.text: The local equation for $C$ in step 5 uses an actual etale neighbourhood, a regular local ring, and a sublist of its regular system of parameters. An affine neighbourhood of $z$ exists because $V$ is a scheme, and its germ map gives precisely this ideal. With the effective Cartier property from step 6, these are all the conditions of [def-trf-normal-crossings-divisor]. Hence $C$ has normal crossings. This assertion permits unlabelled global components of $C$ to self-intersect; the labels are needed for the stricter assertion about $D$.

No two members of $\mathcal G$ contain one another. Different $E_b$ are disjoint and nonempty. For two members from different original labels, a containment would, at any point of the smaller member, give containment of their local hyperplanes. Their ideals are distinct parameter primes, incomparable by [lem-sfb-transverse-prime-ideal-parameters](b), a contradiction. These members are finite, integral and closed, and their union is $|D|$. An irreducible closed subset of a finite union of closed subsets lies in one of them: intersect with each closed subset and use irreducibility, inducting on the number of subsets. Maximality and the preceding noncontainments therefore show that the irreducible components of $D$ are exactly $\mathcal G$. Their reduced structures agree with the prescribed ones by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](3). Steps 3, 4 and 6 now verify every clause of [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]: reduced Cartier ideal, finite distinct integral regular components, and all regular intersections with the required local dimension equality.

source.place: VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), regular intersections of the actual irreducible components.

proof.text: Finally each $G\in\mathcal G$ is a component of $C$. It is an irreducible closed subset of $C$, so lies in a component $T$ of $C$; finiteness and coverage of the component family follow from [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components] applied to the closed subset $|C|\subseteq Y$. Likewise $T$ lies in an irreducible component $W$ of $Y$. By step 2, $W$ is open in $Y$. Since $C$ is effective Cartier, [lem-pc-cartier-divisor-nowhere-dense] says it contains no nonempty open subset; hence $T\subsetneq W$. If $G\subsetneq T$, the chain $G\subsetneq T\subsetneq W$ of irreducible closed subsets would give codimension at least two for $G$ in $Y$, contrary to its singleton codimension one in step 3. Therefore $G=T$. By [def-trf-union-of-irreducible-components], $D$ is a union of components of $C$. If the family is empty this is vacuous. If $Y$ is empty every pointwise condition is vacuous, the ideals of $C,D$ are the unit ideals, and the same proof gives the empty component lists and all the asserted conclusions.
